proposal.reactor_type: Coiled PTFE Tubing with External Heat Exchanger
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Equal molar flow of strong base and organic acid requires immediate mixing to initiate neutralization. A T-junction provides sufficient turbulence for rapid mixing at these flow rates.
pre_reactor_steps: Pre-cool both streams to 0-5 C using external heat exchangers before mixing to manage the adiabatic temperature rise.
Install back-pressure regulator (BPR) downstream of the reactor to maintain pressure and prevent boiling if local hotspots exceed 100 C.
post_reactor_steps: Pass effluent through a secondary heat exchanger to return to ambient temperature (25 C) for safe collection.
Collect product in a vented container.
proposal.chemistry_notes: Neutralization of organic acid with NaOH is highly exothermic (Delta H ~ -55 kJ/mol). Adiabatic rise of 55 C means T_final could reach ~80 C if starting at 25 C. Flow chemistry allows precise heat removal. PTFE is chemically resistant to both acid and base.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Batch completion is <2s. 0.05 min (3s) provides a safety factor of 1.5x while ensuring high throughput.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 10 mL/min total (5+5) is a standard lab-scale flow rate, manageable by syringe pumps.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Target outlet temperature is 25 C. Inlet is pre-cooled to manage exotherm.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Calculated from Flow Rate (10 mL/min) * Residence Time (0.05 min) = 0.5 mL.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID provides high surface-area-to-volume ratio for efficient heat transfer.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 10 bar ensures liquid phase stability and prevents cavitation/boiling during exothermic spike.

proposal.literature_analogies: Standard acid-base neutralization in flow chemistry often uses PTFE or PFA tubing with external cooling jackets or baths to manage exotherms.
safety_flags: Exothermic Reaction: Monitor temperature closely. Ensure cooling bath is active before starting pumps.
Corrosive Materials: NaOH and Organic Acid can cause burns. Use appropriate PPE.
Pressure: System operates at 10 bar. Ensure all fittings are rated for this pressure.
